items.title: PENGUINS: WHEN THE WADDLE WAS SUPERSIZED
items.label: Blogs
items.excerpt:
Their fossil relatives could deliver that expression on a much larger scale.

In 2023, researchers described Kumimanu fordycei, an enormous penguin from New Zealand. Its fossils came from rocks approximately 55–60 million years old, placing it in the Paleocene, relatively soon after the extinction of the non-avian dinosaurs.

Based on comparisons between its bones and those of living penguins, the team estimated a body mass of around 150 kilograms. That is several times the weight of a living emperor penguin.

This was a bird we would politely allow to pass first on a narrow beach.

The remains are incomplete, so its precise standing height is uncertain. A very large wing bone gives researchers useful evidence of its bulk, but it does not supply a complete outline of the animal.

Its flipper bones also retained features different from those of modern penguins, including less flattened shapes. Early penguin evolution was already producing giants while aspects of their swimming…

items.title: 🛢️ Fossil Fuels: 40% of Maritime Shipping Tonnage, 50% of its Fuel Use
items.label: Blogs
items.excerpt:
🫧 Open on Bubbles

Michael Barnard at CleanTechnica :

Fossil fuels are roughly 40% of maritime tonnage, but in the model they represent about half of maritime freight energy because coal, oil, and gas are mostly long-haul bulk trades. Moving a ton of scrap metal a short distance and moving a ton of oil or LNG across oceans are not the same transport-energy problem, even if both show up as one ton in a cargo table.

That distinction matters because shipping fuel demand is driven by transport work, not just tons loaded at ports. Ton-kilometres are the better mental model. Fossil fuel cargoes travel long distances in very large flows, so their decline removes more than a proportional share of cargo mass. It removes a larger share of the ocean work and the fuel burned to do that work.

Escrever usando papel e caneta tem sido terapêutico. Sempre pensei que, para mim, digitar seria a melhor forma de colocar os pensamentos para fora, já que consigo digitar rápido o suficiente para tentar acompanhar meus pensamentos rápidos. Mas surpreendentemente, o que tem funcionado é justamente reduzir a velocidade, escrevendo com calma, me obrigando a tomar o tempo necessário para escrever cada letra no seu devido lugar.

Esse novo momento fez com que eu tentasse melhorar minha caligrafia, algo que venho negligenciando a vários anos.

Escrever com calma, diminuindo o ritmo dos meus pensamentos, acalmar a mente, fazer com que o ato de parar para escrever vire algo rotineiro, uma terapia diária, meu pequeno momento de meditação.

items.title: yes, quicksand is real
items.label: Blogs
items.excerpt:
Up to my waist in quicksand - Pinto Creek, Arizona

One of the great things about Arizona, is there are numerous hidden canyons, ravines, and washes for exploring. One of my favorites is Pinto Creek, near Roosevelt. There is no trail, just the creek that winds through an increasingly narrow canyon.

Pinto Creek, near Roosevelt, Arizona

At one point, there is a beautiful box canyon (see my photo page ) where I have never seen another person, just an occasional footprint.

If you spend enough time exploring these desert canyons, there is a good chance you will encounter quicksand. I used to think quicksand was a myth reserved for episodes of the Lone Ranger and Tarzan . It turns out that it is very real. There have been numerous times I've been treading along a wash, or small stream, only to suddenly drop to my waist in slushy sand.

Aftermath of my most recent encounter with quicksand

items.title: Counting seconds
items.label: Small Web
items.excerpt:
When I brew my coffee, I generally do it in 4 parts. One is the blooming phase, I pour 50ml and wait until it's all gone through.

Then I do three other 50ml pours with 10 seconds between each.

To count these 10 seconds, I use crocodiles, like so: "Un crocodile, deux crocodiles, trois crocodiles,...".

Crocodile is the word we use in the french speaking part of Belgium. I think I have seen Americans use Mississippi as well.

I'll use this note as a way to compile all different manners of counting in seconds from around the world. If you could send me an email to tell me how it's done in your part of the world, I'd be very pleased.

Crocodile: Wallonia

Mississippi: USA

The experiment lives at cdn.jamesst.one, which now serves a copy of this site, and you can watch where it is routing at rum.jamesst.one.

The above diagram is actually a simplification, because before that, a client first has to look up the IP address to connect to, i.e. DNS. A multi-CDN hooks into the DNS reply and picks which CDN is best, then that CDN’s anycast picks which specific data center based on network routing rules.

The CDN is chosen in DNS. When your resolver asks for cdn.jamesst.one, the answer is a CNAME to one of three CDNs, and which one depends on where you are. Or, more accurately, the network you are on.

The first version used a small script on the page that read Resource Timing entries and beaconed them home. It worked, but I would rather not put JS on pages for this. jsDelivr itself gets its RUM data from elsewhere: it used Cedexis, then PerfOps, rather than running a script of its own.

items.title: Let's Play with Hardcaml!
items.label: Small Web
items.excerpt:
I prepared a five-minute lightning talk for the 8th Homebrew CPU Meetup on November 28, 2026. The slides are below.

Open slides in a new tab · Download PDF · View Markdown source

This talk is a gentle introduction to Hardcaml, an RTL design library embedded in OCaml. Rather than discussing advanced verification techniques, I wanted to share the fun of building digital circuits in an interactive programming environment.

We start with a simple 5-bit counter and do everything inside utop, an OCaml REPL:

No FPGA, external Verilog simulator, or even a separate OCaml project is needed to try this example. I tested the installation steps and the REPL session in a Docker environment, so you can follow along with the slides.

With the help of AI coding agents, I ended up building a dual-core RISC-V SoC that boots Linux 6.18 with SMP on a Colorlight i9 FPGA board.

I hope this talk encourages more people to give Hardcaml a try and enjoy building their own digital circuits.

items.title: 75% of Rockstar’s workers have voted against unionizing
items.label: Hobbies and Creative
items.excerpt:
The IWGB, a union representing some Rockstar workers, has confirmed that workers rejected a deal that would recognize the Rockstar Game Workers Union.

The two-week ballot, which ran from 12 to 26 November, overlapped with the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. The results were roughly 25% in favor of recognizing the union, and 75% against, with the vast majority of its around 1,600 employees participating.

Recognition would have established a formal framework for workers to negotiate collectively over pay, overtime, bonuses, leave, pensions, and the impact of AI and redundancies.

The result does not prevent Rockstar workers from organizing with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights, but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives. The union is also able to continue representing individual members.

The IWGB says that this has not dissuaded them, and they will continue to try and “win the trust” of Rockstar employees.

items.title: Toasted coconut on pumpkin pie
items.label: Q&A
items.excerpt:
My family has always served pumpkin pie with whipped cream and toasted coconut. I have never met anyone else who has toasted coconut with their pumpkin pie. Where did they get this from?

Totally standard canned pumpkin, evaporated milk, eggs type pumpkin pie. I have a distinct memory of my grandmother toasting sweetened shredded coconut on a baking sheet in the oven and watching it like a hawk because it burns easily. She's no longer with us so I can't ask her. My dad, her son, has no idea. She was a great baker, but not an experimental one. Child of Polish immigrants, grew up on a farm in Connecticut during the Depression. Primarily a homemaker; later in life worked in a grocery store deli.

Internet searches have been unhelpful because they only bring up pie that uses coconut milk or oil as a dairy alternative.

Any ideas? Anyone else with this tradition? Any other interesting pumpkin pie toppings?

items.excerpt:
Puzzit is your home for free puzzle games online. Play word games, number puzzles, logic games and original Puzzit challenges directly in your browser. No downloads and no sign-up required - just pick a puzzle and start playing

Born from a love of puzzles - we are small passionate team behind
Puzzit started with a simple frustration - great puzzle games were buried under app stores, paywalls, and endless install screens. We believed the best puzzle experience should be one click away, right in your browser.

So we built it. A growing collection of hand-picked casual puzzle games - math crosswords, logic teasers, and more - all free, all instantly playable, all designed to give your brain that satisfying little workout it craves.

items.title: Mailwidget
items.label: Showcase
items.excerpt:
There's a MacOS app called TerminalWidget that can put terminal output in desktop widgets (I'll bet you saw that coming). Mailwidget is a shell script for creating a TerminalWidget that shows the unread count in any Mail.app mailboxes you choose.

There's a fair amount of fiddly configuration involved in making this work right, which is documented in the linked post. I did this to scratch an itch: there used to be utilities that would apply additional unread-count badges to Mail.app's icon, but those are long gone, and I wanted some approximation of that back.

items.title: Feed the Scorchpot [$14.99] [Strategy] [Windows] [macOS]
items.label: Gaming
items.excerpt:
You struck a deal with a dragon: twenty years of protection for twenty years of dinner service. The island thrives under the beast's watchful eye, as long as the meals keep coming.

Every year, the dragon wakes up hungrier. You roll dice to work your island, harvest ingredients, fuse them into recipes, and cook them down in the Scorchpot — the pot you keep full or end up in. Get the meal right and you prosper. Get it wrong and you're smoke.

Build farmsteads, shrines, and harbors across your hex-grid island, each one changing how the board pays out. The best runs start with a handful of tiles and end with a machine that buries the dragon in food. Then the odds tighten, the dragon turns picky, and you tear the whole thing down and rebuild while it's on fire.

Feed the Scorchpot, keep the dragon happy, and outlast the contract.

Cook cleverly, plan badly, or just roll with it — the dragon doesn't care how you win, only that you feed the beast on time. And yes, you can pet the…
